content:
elaine: Heads-up — saw a production hang when token refresh happened mid-stream on the Go client. Short repro below.

matt: ugh, we've hit that before. any logs or a goroutine dump?

elaine: repro steps:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", apiURL+"/v1/stream", body)
resp, err := client.Do(req) // client is runtime's default http.Client with shared transport
// server returns 401 mid-stream -> client triggers refresh -> stream blocks
```

shane: paste the goroutine dump. usually it's resp.Body.Read blocked in net/http2 readLoop while refresh waits on conn pool.

elaine: attached snippet: multiple goroutines in io.read, one in token refresh blocked on transport

linh: this is the common anti-pattern: refresh uses same transport as streaming. If long-lived streams occupy connections, refresh blocks acquiring a conn. Fix is to use a separate auth transport/client.

matt: also check transport knobs: MaxIdleConnsPerHost, MaxConnsPerHost, IdleConnTimeout. Defaults can starve new streams.

elaine: current config: MaxIdleConnsPerHost=10, IdleConnTimeout=5m, MaxConnsPerHost=0

shane: proposal:
- dedicated http.Client/Transport for auth refresh (small pool)
- streaming transport: increase MaxIdleConnsPerHost (e.g., 100)
- set IdleConnTimeout to 60s for streaming
- set short ResponseHeaderTimeout on control plane calls
- ensure ctx cancel closes resp.Body immediately

linh: add: set auth transport MaxIdleConnsPerHost=1-2 to ensure refresh opens fresh conn and doesn't contend.

elaine: example changes in branch: authClient with small transport; streamClient has larger pool; added goroutine-count test and cancellation fix.

matt: also be aware of HTTP/2 server MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS; if server queues streams, client looks like it's hanging. Increasing per-host pool opens more TCP connections and bypasses per-connection stream limits.

shane: consider circuit-breaker around refresh endpoint to prevent thundering herd if auth endpoint is slow.

elaine: added CB and test. opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/512

devex: please add SDK docs warning: "do not reuse transport for auth refresh" with suggested transport settings and code examples.

infra-bot: canary queued — running staging tests :gear:

matt: small review note: make goroutine assertion tolerant; assert goroutine delta < 5 within 2s.

elaine: will update tests per feedback and merge after canary passes. thanks all! :thumbsup:
